history.dynasty: Chera-period minor rulers of Salem (fort builders); renovated 1881; charitable choultry built 1876 by Parvathiyammal and Muthukumara Pillai
history.period: Ancient — reported 500-1000 years old (sources conflict: 'over 500 years' vs '1000 years', Chera era — verify)
history.summary: Kottai Mariamman Temple is the famous guardian-deity temple of Salem city, on the eastern bank of the Thirumanimutharu river in the Fort (Kottai) area of Salem (CSV town 'Salem' is correct; geocode places it on Bazzar Street, 1st Agraharam, Fort, Salem 636001). The goddess is known as Periya Mariamman (the Great Mariamman), and as the foremost of the eight Mariamman temples in Salem city she is regarded as the city's guardian deity. History: when Chera-country minor rulers built a fort and ruled Salem, they built this temple along with a Perumal temple; Mariamman was worshipped by the fort soldiers as guardian deity. The present location on the river's eastern bank is attributed to Kanakasabhai Mudaliar and Siva Sankara Mudaliar, who installed the goddess and performed Kumbabhishekam. An old poem records that when the fort (and Salem) was found, Periya Mari was found there too. Antiquity conflict: sources report 500 to 1000 years. Notable: the small sanctum (devotees bow to enter), the goddess facing northeast (Eesanya) with a lotus bud beneath her feet, nine sculptured pillars in the Sannadhi Mandapam and sculptures of Kali in the Kili Mandapam. Beliefs: the flower-divination rite (right flower chosen = prayer fulfilled), chicken-pox healing with sacred water, and devotees leaving clay models of body parts for cures.

town_description: Salem is a major city in western Tamil Nadu on the Thirumanimutharu river, headquarters of Salem district. The temple stands in the Kottai (fort) area of the old city near the Salem old bus stand, in the heart of Salem city.
